title: Mitigate asymmetric NAT rebinding causing ephemeral hostname drift between dedicated tenants
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: A production customer observed intermittent cross-tenant hostname drift and DNS responses mapping to ephemeral NAT ports owned by a different tenant after a Dedicated pool scale-down. Impacted customers saw short-lived requests attributed to incorrect tenant metadata, causing authorization mismatches and telemetry noise. Repro window is intermittent and correlated with autoscaler scale-down events and certain host kernel versions.

Root cause hypothesis: During scale-down, ephemeral SNAT port reassignment on a small percentage of hosts allowed connection tuples to be reused before control-plane egress labels and conntrack namespace reconciliation completed. A race between the autoscaler, host-level conntrack namespace cleanup, and our eBPF-based egress tagging caused socket marks to be ambiguous for a brief window. Downstream DNS cache heuristics then associated responses with the wrong tenant's egress flow.

Immediate mitigation deployed: 1) emergency runtime flag enabled to bar aggressive conntrack reuse on impacted host pool (hotfix 2.4.1-rc). 2) conservative scale-down window enforced (30s delay) for affected Dedicated clusters. 3) added an interim agent that stamps SNAT mappings with tenant UUID in a persistent nat-metadata map to prevent reuse for 2 minutes post-teardown. These reduced cross-tenant hits to near zero in canary.

Long-term fix plan: 1) implement strict per-tenant conntrack namespaces unlink flow that guarantees in-kernel namespace separation on scale-down. 2) extend eBPF program to carry tenant_mark through full postscale lifecycle and enforce drop of flows without a matching tenant mark. 3) add reconciliation job in control plane to validate SNAT table ownership after host recycle. 4) update autoscaler to await conntrack drain completion before removing a host from rotation.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for eBPF verifier logic and conntrack marker lifecycle, integration tests in dedicated staging with forced scale-in/out loops, canary rollout to 3 Dedicated pools (low-latency customers) with increased telemetry sampling for tenant-egress-crossflow-rate and dns-response-tenant-mismatch.

Rollout plan: Canary -> 25% pool rollout -> full fleet. Rollback path: disable eBPF tenant-enforcement and revert autoscaler delay; revert hotfix flag. All rollouts gated by tenant-egress-crossflow-rate metric and customer-reported errors.

Observability additions: New alerts and dashboards: tenant-egress-crossflow-rate, snat-orphan-count, conntrack-reconcile-lag, dns-anomaly-rate, per-tenant egress-socket-mark-mismatch.

Customer comms: Notified affected customers with incident timeline and mitigation steps on 2026-02-26; follow-up scheduled after full rollout.

Postmortem actions: Add regression tests to CI simulating scale-down with heavy NAT churn, schedule audit for host kernel versions in Dedicated fleets, and add runbook entry for similar future escalations.
